Agdaagux Tribe of King Cove

The Agdaagux Tribe of King Cove is an Alaska Native tribal government based in King Cove on the south side of the Alaska Peninsula. The Tribe’s own site identifies its Tribal Council. The Aleutian Pribilof Islands Association describes King Cove as a community shaped by Unangan fishing traditions, people moving from other villages, and a cannery built in 1911.

01

The Tribe and King Cove

The Tribe identifies its Tribal Council on its official site and lists its address in King Cove, Alaska. The Aleutian Pribilof Islands Association locates the town on the south side of the Alaska Peninsula, across the water from Deer Island.

Read the sources [1] Agdaagux Tribe of King Cove [2] Aleutian Pribilof Islands Association

02

The cannery and the families who came to King Cove

Pacific American Fisheries built a salmon cannery at King Cove in 1911. The regional association’s accounts describe workers and families arriving from nearby villages, including Belkofski, Sanak and False Pass. Its history of King Cove records a 1976 fire and subsequent rebuilding.

Read the sources [2] Aleutian Pribilof Islands Association [3] Aleutian Pribilof Islands Association

03

Remembering Belkofski in King Cove

When families moved from Belkofski to King Cove, they brought church bells and icons with them. The Orthodox Church in America documents how residents and the Belkofski Tribal Council helped bring the bells back into use at Saint Herman Church in 2016.

Read the sources [4] Aleutian Pribilof Islands Association [5] Orthodox Church in America

04

Language, art, and public celebrations

The Aleutian Pribilof Islands Association gives the Unangam Tunuu name Agdaaĝux̂ for King Cove and credits Lucy Kenezuroff of Belkofski for the pronunciation recording. Tribal member Sean Mack writes about making a beaded glass float on an Aleutian research expedition. The Aleutians East Borough documents the King Cove Unangan Dancers performing at the school during a 2022 visit.

Read the sources [3] Aleutian Pribilof Islands Association [6] NOAA Ocean Exploration [9] Aleutians East Borough

05

Environmental work and local knowledge

The Tribe’s environmental department describes monitoring water and shellfish and working with local youth on environmental education. Liza Mack’s dissertation examines how Eastern Aleutian leaders learn about and respond to rules affecting access to local resources.

Read the sources [8] Agdaagux Tribe of King Cove [7] University of Alaska Fairbanks

What needs further research

  • More Agdaagux-authored oral histories and dated community accounts could deepen the guide’s coverage of fishing, language, and local history.
